record.paper_title: Some of my favorite open problems
record.context_brief: Uniform summation process for degree recovery
record.original_question: Does there exist, for each p>3, a summation process (σ_{n,ε}) depending only on p such that for every f∈W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1) one can recover the degree from the Fourier magnitudes by lim_{ε→0}\sum_{n∈Z} n|a_n(f)|^2 σ_{n,ε}=deg f? Likewise, for each Hölder exponent α≤1/3, does there exist such a summation process depending only on α that works for every f∈C^{0,α}(S^1;S^1)?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 5.6. Given any p > 3 (resp., α ≤ 1/3), does there exist a summation process (σn,ε), depending only on p (resp., α) such that (5.13) holds for every f ∈ W1/p,p (resp., f ∈ C0,α)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^1 = \{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z|=1\}$. For a measurable map $f : S^1 \to S^1$, denote by $a_n(f) = \frac{1}{2\pi}\int_{S^1} f(\theta) e^{-in\theta}\,d\theta$, $n \in \mathbb{Z}$, its Fourier coefficients. When $f$ is sufficiently regular (for example $f \in W^{1/2,2}(S^1;S^1)$), the topological degree of $f$ admits the representation
$$\deg f \;=\; \sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} n\,|a_n(f)|^2.$$
For less regular $f$ the series above is generally not convergent, and one looks for a regularization by means of a summation process. A summation process is a family $(\sigma_{n,\varepsilon})_{n\in\mathbb{Z},\,\varepsilon>0}$ of real numbers, depending on a parameter $\varepsilon>0$, such that for each $\varepsilon>0$ the weighted series $\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} n\,|a_n(f)|^2\,\sigma_{n,\varepsilon}$ converges absolutely (for the considered class of $f$) and one studies the limit as $\varepsilon\to 0$.

For $s\in(0,1)$ and $p\in[1,\infty)$, let $W^{s,p}(S^1;S^1)$ denote the fractional Sobolev space of $S^1$-valued maps, and for $\alpha\in(0,1]$ let $C^{0,\alpha}(S^1;S^1)$ denote the space of $\alpha$-Hölder continuous $S^1$-valued maps. Both classes consist of continuous maps and so the topological degree $\deg f \in \mathbb{Z}$ is well defined.

Questions:

(a) For each real number $p > 3$, does there exist a summation process $(\sigma_{n,\varepsilon})$ depending only on $p$ such that
$$\lim_{\varepsilon \to 0}\;\sum_{n\in\mathbb{Z}} n\,|a_n(f)|^2\,\sigma_{n,\varepsilon} \;=\; \deg f$$
holds for every $f \in W^{1/p,p}(S^1;S^1)$?

(b) For each Hölder exponent $\alpha \in (0,1/3]$, does there exist a summation process $(\sigma_{n,\varepsilon})$ depending only on $\alpha$ such that the same identity holds for every $f \in C^{0,\alpha}(S^1;S^1)$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem in a 2023 collection of favorite open problems by Brezis. Searches did not turn up any subsequent paper resolving it; related works on degree formulas for circle-valued maps (and recent solutions of other problems on the list) do not address this specific summation-process question, so it appears to remain open.
